init.title: U-tec Locks options
init.description: The polling interval cannot be lower than 30 seconds. Push needs Home Assistant Cloud or an external HTTPS URL.

data.slow_poll_when_push_healthy: Slow down polling while push is healthy

data_description.poll_interval: 30 to 3,600 seconds. 30 seconds is the minimum and cannot be lowered.
data_description.use_push: Needs Home Assistant Cloud (Nabu Casa) or an external HTTPS URL. Plain HTTP is never used for push.
data_description.slow_poll_when_push_healthy: Poll less often while push is proven to deliver changes. Returns to the normal interval at the first missed change.
data_description.push_healthy_poll_interval: 60 to 1,800 seconds (recommended 120). Only used with the option above.
data_description.confirm_commands: Up to 10 quick checks over about 56 seconds after each of your lock, unlock or mode commands.

conflicting_integration.title: U-tec Locks blocked by the u_tec integration
conflicting_integration.description: The legacy `{domain}` integration is loaded. Running both on one U-tec account doubles API requests and they take push from each other, so U-tec Locks will not set up. Disable or remove `{domain}`, then reload U-tec Locks.

push_unhealthy.title: U-tec push notifications are not working
push_unhealthy.description:
For the last 24 hours U-tec push has not delivered lock changes (or could not be registered). Lock state can lag behind changes made at the lock or in the U-tec app by up to the polling interval. Polling continues as normal.

Check that Home Assistant Cloud is connected, or that your external HTTPS URL is reachable from the internet. This repair clears itself when push is healthy again.

push_no_https_url.title: No HTTPS URL for U-tec push
push_no_https_url.description:
Push notifications are on, but Home Assistant has no Home Assistant Cloud webhook and no external HTTPS URL. Push is only ever registered over HTTPS because the push secret travels in a request header.

Set up Home Assistant Cloud, or set an external HTTPS URL under Settings → System → Network, then reload U-tec Locks. Everything keeps working on polling in the meantime. You can also turn push off in the integration options.

rate_limited.title: U-tec is rate limiting requests
rate_limited.description: U-tec answered with "too many requests" three or more times in the last hour. The integration is backing off. Check the API request sensors on the U-tec account device, and consider a longer polling interval. This repair clears after 24 hours without rate limiting.

command_loop.title: Many commands sent to {name}
command_loop.description: {count} lock commands were sent to {name} within 10 minutes. This often means an automation is fighting the lock's auto-lock. If you want the door to stay unlocked, use the Lock mode select and choose Passage instead. Commands are never blocked.

lock_removed.title: {name} is no longer on your U-tec account

confirm.title: Remove {name}?
confirm.description: {name} was missing from the last two U-tec discoveries, so its entities are unavailable. If you removed it from the Xthings Home app (or deselected it under OpenAPI), submit to delete the device from Home Assistant. If it comes back, it will be added again automatically.
